signature.instructions:
text
TASK: Visual diff + discard/keep classification for an image pair.
- Image 1 = original
- Image 2 = updated (reimage)

YOU MAY RECEIVE
A) Two images (image_original and image_reimage), or
B) Only one image (the other is None/missing).

OUTPUT (ABSOLUTE)
Return ONLY one JSON object (no markdown, no reasoning):
{"discard_image": true/false, "changes": "<string>"}

PRIMARY GOAL
1) Decide whether this pair should be DISCARDED (discard_image=true) or KEPT (discard_image=false).
2) If kept, describe only CLEAR, MEANINGFUL visual/content changes.
3) Be extremely conservative: if you cannot clearly verify a difference, treat as no meaningful change.

DEFAULT ASSUMPTION
Start from:
{"discard_image": true, "changes": "Images are identical - no changes"}
Deviate only when rules below force it.

------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 — CLASSIFY EACH IMAGE AS INFORMATIONAL vs NON‑INFORMATIONAL
NON‑INFORMATIONAL (usually discard):
- Any content that is ONLY branding/logos/icons/wordmarks/slogans with no document-like information.
  This includes:
  - Single corporate logos/wordmarks (e.g., GM, Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, Cadillac).
  - “Logo collages” (multiple brand marks together).
  - Facility/marketing lockups/slogans such as “Canadian Technical Centre / INNOVATION LIVES HERE”, “GENERAL MOTORS CANADA”, etc.
  - Watermark-only pages like “GM Confidential”.
- Blank blocks/solid rectangles, divider lines, standalone section numbers.
Key lesson from evaluation: “Canadian Technical Centre INNOVATION LIVES HERE” should be treated as NON‑INFORMATIONAL (branding/marketing), even though it contains words.

INFORMATIONAL (keep if it’s the only image; compare if both):
- Readable sentences/paragraphs conveying document content.
- Tables, charts, diagrams/flowcharts with labeled parts that communicate technical/process information.
- Legends with labeled items that describe something beyond branding (e.g., a list like “Fastboot / ADB / OTG – Carplay / QFIL for virgin board flashing” is informational).

When uncertain, bias toward NON‑INFORMATIONAL for logo/slogan-only images.

------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 2 — HANDLE ONE‑IMAGE CASES (other image is None)
If only ONE image is provided:
- If NON‑INFORMATIONAL:
  {"discard_image": true, "changes": "Only one image which is non-informational and it contains only logo/watermark/blank block/single line/standalone section number"}
- If INFORMATIONAL:
  {"discard_image": false, "changes": "NoMatchFound"}

------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 3 — HANDLE TWO‑IMAGE CASES
A) BOTH NON‑INFORMATIONAL (logos/watermarks/branding/slogans only), regardless of differences:
{"discard_image": true, "changes": "Both images are non informational and contain only logos / etc.."}

B) ONE INFORMATIONAL, ONE NON‑INFORMATIONAL:
KEEP the pair:
{"discard_image": false, "changes": "OVERVIEW: Only one image is informational. | DETAILS (Each Change): 1) Image <1 or 2> contains <brief description of meaningful content>; the other image is non-informational (logo/blank/etc.)."}

C) BOTH INFORMATIONAL:
- If identical or only trivial differences => DISCARD:
  {"discard_image": true, "changes": "Images are identical - no changes"}
- If meaningful differences exist => KEEP and use the template below.

------------------------------------------------------------
MEANINGFUL vs TRIVIAL DIFFERENCES
TRIVIAL (treat as identical; discard):
- Blur/quality/resolution/compression changes where underlying content is the same.
- Minor color shade shifts.
- Layout shifts/resizing/cropping that does NOT add/remove information.
- Watermark/logo added/removed if it does not alter informational content.
- Punctuation-only or tiny spelling variations ONLY if you can read both perfectly and meaning is unchanged.

MEANINGFUL (keep and report):
- Words/numbers/dates/labels added/removed/replaced (must quote old vs new).
- Table structure changes (rows/columns added/removed) or cell value changes.
- Diagram/flowchart elements added/removed/reconnected; label changes.
- Any crossing-out/strike-through that invalidates an informational area.

CROSSED-OUT RULE (override):
If either image clearly has a big X/strike-through crossing out the whole image:
{"discard_image": false, "changes": "Image 1 has been crossed out"} OR "Image 2 has been crossed out"

CORRUPTION / UNREADABLE:
If either image is corrupted/too tiny/too blurry such that you cannot reliably compare:
{"discard_image": false, "changes": "Could not infer"}

------------------------------------------------------------
TEXT CHANGE REPORTING (STRICT NON‑HALLUCINATION)
Before claiming ANY text change:
1) Locate the same region in both images.
2) Read the exact string in Image 1 and Image 2.
3) If you cannot read BOTH perfectly, do NOT claim a text change.
4) If different, quote both strings verbatim: old (Image 1) vs new (Image 2).

Never infer intent, never “fix” spelling, never guess.

------------------------------------------------------------
CHANGES FIELD TEMPLATE (ONLY when meaningful differences exist)
"OVERVIEW: <summary of broad change.> | DETAILS (Each Change): 1) <location/area>: <what changed, quoting exact old (Image 1) and exact new (Image 2) text/values when text is involved>; 2) ..."

Remember: output ONLY the JSON object.
